baby: Your pregnancy starts from the first day of menstruation, which will be your last until your due date. The hormonal changes stimulate the active follicle to mature in the ovaries. As the menstrual cycle continues, the follicles stop growing - except for the dominant one, which will continue to grow. This particular follicle will wait until ovulation, when it will release an egg (oocyte) ready for fertilization.
mom: It's your first week, so you are not pregnant yet- the early symptoms of pregnancy will appear later.
helpful_tips: Start taking prenatal vitamins with folic acid to support your pregnancy. Don't forget to consult a doctor before taking any vitamins.

baby: The follicle resembles a bubble, filled with liquid containing a maturing oocyte. The follicle is recognizable, as it has a bigger size than the others, and is closer to the surface of the ovaries. After ovulation, the dominant follicle goes through all the stages of maturation and the others resorb (undergo atresia). The oocyte is viable for approximately 24 hours after ovulation - this time being the most important factor for conception to be successful.
mom: You might have mild discomfort in the lower abdomen, and increased vaginal discharge during ovulation. Your body temperature might be slightly elevated; and nausea and fatigue may occur due to hormonal changes and progesterone secretion.
helpful_tips: Try to predict when ovulation begins, as this period increases your chances of getting pregnant. For conception to be successful, you need to avoid all methods of contraception, and you should give extra attention to intimate relations with your partner.

baby: Your egg has met one of the million spermatozoids- fertilization has begun. When the spermatozoid reaches its target and dissolves in the oocyte, it passes in all the genetic information of the future child's father. At this point, the fertilized egg might have split into two (three) and you may have identical twins. This is a significant period for you and your baby because each and every one of their organs and systems have already started to develop.
mom: Early symptoms of pregnancy, such as mild nausea, lower abdominal pain, increased sensitivity and breast pain can happen during this period. A heightened sense of smell, changes in taste, and frequent urination can also be some of the early signs of pregnancy.
helpful_tips: From now on, you need to be careful with physical exercise. You shouldn't eat snacks or sugary cereals. Depending on your body, you may have vaginal discharge this week, if its colour has an unpleasant smell or you're unsure about it, you should see your doctor.

baby: The fertilised oocyte embeds into the uterine walls, and rapid cell division takes place. The oocyte turns into an embryo.The first layer (endoderm) forms the inner organs, such as the digestive system, lungs and liver; the second layer (mesoderm) develops the kidneys, heart, muscles, spine, and gonads; and the third layer (ectoderm) initiates the formation of external organs such as hair, skin, eyes, nose and ears. The cells of these layers form chorion, amnion and the yolk sac. Chorion forms the placenta; amnion turns into the amniotic sac; and the yolk sac will perform nutritional functions and hematopoiesis until the foetal organs take over these functions themselves. Your baby is as big as a poppy seed.
mom: Breast tenderness and size could increase. Your body is working with an additional load now, which means you are probably going to get tired faster than usual. Increased irritability, fatigue, mood swings and nervousness accompany the other symptoms this week.
helpful_tips: If you notice light bleeding (spotting) don't worry, as this is normal. However, if you have profuse discharge and constant lower abdominal pain, then you should consult your doctor.If you have already taken a pregnancy test and the result was negative, and you still haven't had your period yet, you shouldn't worry - the level of hCG in your urine is still low. Don't take any painkillers to relieve abdominal pain until you're sure of your pregnancy status. Wait until the end of this or the fifth week and retake the test.

baby: Your baby is growing and changing, and resembles a tadpole.The baby already has a heart in a curved-tube shape, which will later become four-chambered. A crucial moment happens approximately on day 21 - the small heart starts to beat for the first time. From now on, it won't stop beating for a minute. Even features of the head, such as eye dots and pits marking the ears are already showing; and limb buds are sprouting from the embryo trunk.
mom: Your body is changing, and now you can feel it. Morning sickness can occur at any time, day or night; and sometimes it's not that simple to manage. Different triggers such as the smell of food being prepared or even just the thought of it can provoke nausea.The mood swings, dizziness, irritability, and fatigue may get worse, and you might have some doubts about your role as a mother. But please don't worry! All these emotions are absolutely normal and common for pregnant women.
helpful_tips: From now on,you need to take into consideration another person because your bad habits can have a greater impact on your baby than on you.Live a healthy lifestyle, walk outside, and remember that whatever is healthy for you will most likely be beneficial to your baby.If youy haven't visited the doctor yet, then now's the timw to go and have a proper consulation.

baby: Your baby is continuing to develop intensely. The heart hasn't fully developed yet, so the liver fulfils the function of blood formation and circulating it to the heart.During this period, the brain develops - including the formation of the right and left hemispheres; and the brain gyrus and cavities. The legs and arms sprout, and by the end of the week, the beginnings of fingers and toes start to form. At this stage, the face begins to form, and the beginnings of the eyes, nose, mouth and ears will appear.
mom: Your breasts are going to get bigger and give some tingling and burning sensations. This is how the body prepares the mammary glands to adapt your newborn to breastfeeding. Even though your waistline hasn't expanded much, the uterus is growing larger and pushing down on the bladder, causing frequent urination. You may notice a slight gain in weight or even weight loss due to intense morning sickness and vomiting. You may feel increased tiredness, drowsiness and decreased attention, as your body adapts to the demands of pregnancy, increased energy use and your baby growing. Mild headaches, dizziness and mood swings are typical for this stage of pregnancy.
helpful_tips: Try to eat small portions but more often. Take vitamins and drink fresh, organic juices. If you have frequent vomiting, try to drink more fluids to avoid dehydration. Avoid greasy food completely.And it's probably best to put your favourite perfume away during your pregnancy.

baby: The face and head develop continuously. The baby's head is still bent towards the body, but it will gradually start to straighten out and wiggle.The jaw and beginnings of the teeth begin to form. The heart is developing more and more; it has divided into left and right auricular; and by the end of the week, the four-chambered heart will supply the vessels and organs with blood. The umbilical cord, which transfers oxygen and nutrients from your body to your baby - and also excretes waste products from your baby, starts to form. The respiratory system, lungs, kidneys and intestines continue to develop.
mom: You've lost appetite due to morning sickness, although sometimes you feel the urge to try something unusual. Don't be upset about it though, as practice shows, morning sickness disappears after the 13th week. You might feel growing discomfort in your usual clothes, as your body changes for your baby's growth and development.
helpful_tips: If you're still suffering from morning sickness, try adding foods to your diet that will make you thirsty, such as pickles or crackers.Try to eat fruit and vegetables rich in vitamins daily and of course, don't forget about meat, fish and dairy.You should consider changing your wardrobe. It's better to give preference to clothes for everyday wear which are more comfortable; but which aren't tight and won't restrict your movement. If you're worried about abdominal pain or bleeding and you have frequent vomiting, then you should see a doctor.

baby: By the end of the second month all the organs are formed and continue to develop and grow - many having already become functional.Your baby is already starting to move from time to time, but is still too tiny for you to feel the movements. The gonads are developing: boys will have testicles, and girls - ovaries.Even though it has already been determined, it is still too early to find out your baby's sex with an ultrasound. You might be carrying twins, and if so, then it's completely possible for you to have both a girl and a boy.
mom: The growing uterus puts pressure on the organs nearby: the stomach and intestines. And now you're going to have to grapple with uncomfortable sensations such as heartburn.Your breasts increase in size and become more tender and slightly painful; the veins becoming more noticeable due to increased blood flow.There might be some changes to your skin as well: in some cases, it will clear up; whereas in other rashes, peeling, or pigmentation may occur. It's normal for pregnancy, and it usually goes away without any intervention. But if it bothers you, you might want to consult with a dermatologist.
helpful_tips: If you suffer from heartburn, try to reduce or avoid greasy, spicy and fried food and chocolate from your diet. Its best to aviod caffeine and fuzzy soft drinks (soda) at least for now. You should eat slowly and chew throughly; don't overeat, and don't eat before bed.Look after yourself with physical exercise, try not to lift heavy objects and try to stand less.

baby: The embryo is resembling a person more and more. The head is unusually big because of the accelerated growth of the brain.Your baby is developing rapidly and has already learnt to excrete waste products through the umbilical cord to your body by itself.
mom: You may still feel fatigued and a loss of life force energy. In addition to aching breasts, you may notice darkening and swelling of your nipples.Your baby is constantly sending specific signals to your body of what it needs, causing unexpected cravings and an interest to try unusual and peculiar food. You may notice that your skin and hair are becoming drier because your baby requires more water than before. To solve this, you need to increase your water intake, and eat more fresh fruits and vegetables.
helpful_tips: Try to avoid stressful situations. Learn how to keep calm in different situations in life. If you're feeling sad, try to do something entertaining that will make you happy. Don't forget about rest, as during pregnancy your body wastes a lot of energy, therefore, it needs more time to rest and restore itself.

baby: The formation of all organs and systems is completing, and they will develop further. Your baby's skeleton, joints and muscles have already fully developed.Although you won't see your baby's first teeth until six months after they're born, their milk teeth are starting to form now.
mom: The uterus has increased in size and keeps pushing on the bladder, increasing the urge to urinate more often. Excess abdominal and chest hair growth may occur due to the increasing levels of hormones. There might be a dark line on the abdomen which runs from your navel down to the pubic area. Also, pigmentation spots may appear on your face. Don't panic, as it will disappear by itself after you give birth.
helpful_tips: Your baby is continuing to grow, and their development is dependent on your lifestyle. If you are suffering from morning sickness, you don't have to restrict your diet. If you want to eat something, in particular, don't deny yourself. To avoid bringing harm to you and your baby, you shouldn't eat unhealthy foods, such as: alcohol, spicy food, uncooked meat, and sweets.. You can go to the swimming pool, as swimming can be good for your health.

baby: The body of the baby is becoming well proportioned. The cervical vertebrae (spine) become stronger, and now the baby can lift their head up.The hands are developing rapidly, generating the grasp reflex, and your baby is already trying to grab the umbilical cord with its hands. The baby already has a sense of smell by now. Your baby is learning to recognize and remember the smell of the food you eat. The other organs continue to develop.
mom: Your hormones are beginning to settle down.In the meantime, the uterus is expanding as the baby grows, reaching the abdominal cavity and putting less pressure on the bladder.Increased blood flow in your body can cause you to feel hot and have hot flushes, and therefore, your urge to drink more fluids increases, which can result in excessive sweating. You might also notice excessive vaginal discharge. No need to worry about it though, as this is normal and can last the whole pregnancy. But you must see a doctor immediately if you have growing lower abdominal pain, bleeding, and brown coloured and unpleasant-smelling vaginal discharge.
helpful_tips: Your body needs a healthy and fully-nutritious diet. Try to eat more fruits and vegetables, especially raw. If possible, include dairy, fish and lean meat in your diet. If your haemoglobin level is low, you need to eat liver, beef, pomegranate, apples and nuts. It's not recommended to drink coffee, strong tea or alcoholic drinks. Also, you need to avoid significant amounts of pastries and chocolate.Don't forget about going for walks outside, especially before bedtime. It will make you relax and fall asleep more easily.

baby: Your baby has already learnt to put their thumb in their mouth and to swallow amniotic fluid, which they later excrete as urine. The amniotic fluid replenishes itself every day, and is approximately 50 ml in volume at this point. The pituitary gland located in the lower part of the brain starts to secrete hormones for growth, the metabolism, and reproductive function of the baby. The first hairs appear on their body. Your baby's fully formed gonads can now be picked up on an ultrasound; but no need to hurry, as they are still tiny right now, and it's still possible to make mistakes at this point.
mom: Generally, you're feeling much better by this week. You feel less tired and aggressive. Your appetite is coming back, sometimes twice as much. If you had weight loss due to morning sickness before, then now you're going to gain some weight.Breast pain has almost gone away, but your breasts keep getting bigger in preparation to lactate.The development of stretch marks on the abdomen can also cause itchy skin in this area. As the uterus goes up, pressure on the bladder releases, but it starts to press on the intestines, causing other symptoms, such as bloating and constipation.
helpful_tips: If morning sickness is making it harder for you to eat, try to eat foods which you don't react negatively to and which you can digest. You'll soon be feeling better and able to bounce back. In this week, there are no contraindications to intercourse unless you are at risk of miscarriage, having a multiple birth or have a low-lying placenta. But if your pregnancy is normal, then you needn't restrict yourself from this pleasure.

baby: The active growth phase has started. Your baby's body becomes more proportioned. Bone tissue is developing; the limbs are getting longer; the ribs are forming; and the skull and spine are strengthening. The brain is actively growing and increasing in size, and new reflexes and skills appear by the day.Baby girls have oocytes, which already number about several million. And boys have a developing prostate gland.The milk teeth have finally formed, and they're now waiting for the right time to come out. Your baby can already recognise the smell and taste of the food you eat. The mimic muscles are also developing. So now they can move their mouth, express their first emotions, frown, yawn and even smile.
mom: Your body has produced all the necessary hormones to protect your baby. If you suffered morning sickness before, now it will start to fade away and eventually disappear. The expanding uterus is gradually moving from the pelvic to the abdominal cavity, so if you haven't already got one, then now you're going to have a baby bump. Your breasts are noticeably bigger now, and if you squeeze your nipples, yellowish fluid (colostrum) might come out. Don't worry though, as nipple discharge - as well as its absence, is absolutely normal during pregnancy.
helpful_tips: Don't forget to go for walks outside regularly.Walking outside - together with healthy nutrition, contributes to the normal intestinal peristalsis function, helping to prevent constipation that can often occur now. You will notice that after going for a walk, your mood will lift and you'll feel more energetic. All of these will be beneficial for your baby's mood and development.

baby: Your baby's face becomes more natural. The eyes and ears are in place; the neck has straightened up; and the chin lifts. There are features on your baby's face which resemble yours and your partner's.The internal organs are functioning in a more coordinated way. Each day your baby improves their skills and learns to control their movements.
mom: Morning sickness is replaced by lower back pain caused by weight gain and your centre of gravity shifting. You might be constantly hungry, as your baby and its' need for nutrients are actively growing. Your immune system may be compromised as a result of vitamin deficiency in your body. Your skin becomes dry and starts to peel. Vitamin deficiency can make your hair and nails brittle and dry. Also, your gums might bleed, and be sore and sensitive. That's why you shouldn't forget to nourish yourself with nutrients -including vitamins for pregnant women.
helpful_tips: Your belly becomes more prominent this week. Therefore, you need to be careful and avoid accidental injury. Your movements should be smooth and slow. If you drive, don't forget to fasten your seatbelt. Don't open your car windows, to avoid breathing in polluted air. If you want to exercise, try going swimming or exercising on a cross-trainer.

baby: Your baby's tiny heart continues to circulate blood around their entire body. By the way, your baby's heart rate is two times faster than your own. Their kidneys work actively and their bladder is emptied regularly.The pituitary gland is now fully developed, and your baby's future development will continue thanks to pituitary hormone secretion. The body stretches; the arms and legs continue to grow; the legs are getting longer than arms; and the baby themself looks more like a human now.If you are having a boy, then the hormone testosterone is being produced at this point. It is namely this hormone that is responsible for masculine features.
mom: Depending on your skin type, pigmentation might intensify, and any existing freckles and moles might become darker by a few shades. The areolae increase in size and also become darker. Don't worry though, as these changes will go away after birth. You might become more distracted and absent-minded due to hormonal changes. It's not rare to have a stuffy nose, which is a symptom of rhinitis. If you have this condition, then you might also have other symptoms, such as sneezing, an itchy nose and even coughing. Sometimes you might have headaches. You don't have to worry, as rhinitis isn't a threat to you or your baby - it will only cause slight discomfort. But still, it might be a good idea to consult your doctor about the stuffy nose and its possible cause.
helpful_tips: As your belly grows, it becomes harder to sleep in the usual positions.It's not recommended to sleep on your back, as this position can increase pressure on the inferior vena cava. It can interrupt blood flow from the lower limbs, uterus and rectum, which can lead to a very common complication that pregnant women have - varicose veins of the lower limbs and rectum (haemorrhoids).

baby: Your baby doesn't pass up on the opportunity to practice, and from time to time they wince, make faces, and learn to wink.Your baby's bone marrow is now responsible for blood formation; the blood compounds are fully formed; and it's now possible to determine your baby's blood group and rhesus factor. If you are having a girl, her uterus forms at this point; and her ovaries already have over five million oocytes - each one of which could potentially become your grandson or granddaughter and make you a grandparent.Boys have developed a penis and testicles, but the testicles haven't descended into the scrotum yet and are still in the abdominal cavity.
mom: During this week you might feel your baby's first kicks or quickening. From now on you begin to your role as a mother. These movements can be easily misinterpreted though - especially if it's your first pregnancy. With the growth of your uterus pressing on other organs, you might feel mild abdominal pain. This pain might also be caused by bloating and constipation due to inadequate nutrition. That's why you should reconsider your diet, by including healthy and nutritious, fibre-rich foods which have a laxative effect. Sharp, cramp-like pain in the lower abdomen might be a sign of elevated uterine tone. To deal with it, you need to lie down and relax. If after doing this you still suffer from the pain, you need to see a doctor immediately.
helpful_tips: Raw fish and other uncooked products can cause infectious disease. That is why you should exclude foods like these from your diet during pregnancy. Do you remember that high heels are not compatible with pregnancy? Don't forget it. High heels shoes can cause varicose veins, which won't do any good for you or your baby.

baby: The subcutaneous fat is forming, which will be responsible for heat exchange in your future baby's body. Your baby's body is now covered in a thin layer of skin, and their body is maintained at the right temperature by downy fetal hair (lanugo) which covers their whole body and retains the waxy substance on their skin.Your baby can hear sounds surrounding them very well - not just from within your body, but from outside too. You can start talking to you baby now, as they can remember your voice and even recognize it right after being born.
mom: Your cardiac load has increased, because your heart has to work for two bodies at the same time. The whole circulatory system has to work harder, putting more tension on the blood vessels and capillaries. It may result in mild nosebleeds and bleeding gums. As the uterus grows, the ligaments which support the growing placenta stretch. It might cause discomfort or stabbing pain in the lower abdomen on one or both sides.When pain occurs, try laying down and avoid making any sudden movements. If you like sleeping on your front, you'll have to hold off from that while you're pregnant, as it could increase pressure on your womb.
helpful_tips: Your future child is actively taking calcium from your body. A deficiency in this element can lead to problems with foetal development and your own body. That's why you must include calcium-rich products to your diet.

baby: Your baby keeps growing, and their body becomes more proportional. The arms and legs, phalanges of the fingers and even fingerprints completely unique to them are completely formed. Even though their eyes are still closed, your baby reacts to well light coming in through your belly, and even squints when it is bright. The immune system is finishing its development.Earlier, it was your antibodies which performed any immune response and protection, but now your baby can do it by itself. Regardless of whether you're having a boy or girl, your baby's gonads are fully developed, and ultrasound can now determine your baby's sex precisely.
mom: The foetus has grown, so the size of your womb has also increased. Your belly has become more prominent and rounder, and it's harder to hide it now than before. As your body gains weight and your centre of gravity shifts, your gait and posture will also change. You might have lower back pain. The increased load on the cardiovascular system may result in raised blood pressure. You may also experience some dizziness, especially after sudden head movements.
helpful_tips: When morning sickness has gone, the appetite of many pregnant women starts to boost and they gain weight. Now it's essential to check your menu so that you don't gain excess weight. Your diet should contain all the vitamins, elements and proteins that are necessary for the normal development of your baby. You should limit or cut out spicy, greasy and fried foods from your diet. Do exercises and strengthen your pelvic muscles. These exercises will help you during labour.

baby: The brain is still maturing rapidly. The connection between the nervous and muscular systems is improving, and your baby's movements are becoming more balanced and focused.The sebaceous glands work harder, and your baby's body is covered in vernix which protects them from harmful microorganisms and from being pickled by the amniotic fluid. Your baby is moving around energetically, constantly changing their position. They will turn more than once. Their movements are becoming more noticeable to you, although they may feel like soft and tender strokes as your baby is still small and the amniotic fluid softens the intensity of their kicks.
mom: Your bump is showing now. Your skin will become more sensitive, and your hair may be brittle and dull or, on the contrary, shiny and thick. At this stage, the hip joints are relaxed and begin to loosen.The uterus keeps growing and pushing on your internal organs, causing heartburn and an uncomfortable feeling in the abdomen. Foetal growth may cause mild discomfort in the navel region. If this isn't your first pregnancy, you can probably already feel your baby quickening. But if it is your first pregnancy and you haven't felt your baby quickening yet don't worry, you maybe didn't notice it, or confused it with something else.
helpful_tips: Getting sick right now is the last thing you need - even the common cold will cause you a lot of trouble. Fresh air will help you to fight disease. Besides, after a walk in the fresh air, it will be easier for you to fall asleep.Music can help lift your mood and loosen you up. You could sing and dance - the baby will like it.

baby: You're halfway there. Almost every organ has fully developed and is functioning well by now. The head is still quite big, but its size becomes more and more proportional.Your baby's quickening becomes more noticeable and pronounced; they move intensively, trying to grab parts of its body with their fingers and pulling on its umbilical cord. They wave their hands and legs, and the ultrasound can show you how your baby sucks on their thumb or clenches their fists.
mom: The growing uterus starts to push on your belly button from the inside. So you might feel mild discomfort in the navel region from time to time, and your belly button might pop out.
helpful_tips: You can buy a bandage to support your growing belly. You can wear it from the fourth-fifth month of pregnancy. The right bandage will gently support your ever-growing belly; decrease back tension; decrease pressure on your internal organs and blood vessels; and will help your baby to take up the right position.However, it's best to consult your doctor about the necessity of having a bandage before buying one.

baby: The G.I. tract continues to develop and prepare to work independently. Your baby is swallowing amniotic fluid, training the organs of the digestive tract to work and also supply itself with essential nutrients. By the way, the taste and quality of the fluid depend on your lifestyle and diet.There's still plenty of space in the uterus for movement and flips, so don't expect your baby to stay in the same position for a long time. These movements appear especially at night when you just want to relax and sleep.
mom: Knowing that you mustn't sleep on your back and abdomen, the only option left is to sleep on your side, which isn't the most comfortable thing on earth. In addition to this, you might be struggling with frequent urination and heartburn.Constipation also hasn't disappeared, therefore you need to keep an eye on your nutrition. You could also have dizziness and fatigue due to low blood pressure. On the bright side, your emotional health is getting better, so you might experience a lot of pleasant moments as well, such as your baby's quickening. If flutters in your belly made you hesitate before, now you won't have any doubts.
helpful_tips: Avoid stress and trepidation. Throughout the whole of your pregnancy, you need to try and stay calm. If some stressful situations arise, try to react calmly. All you need to worry about is your own health and your baby's development. Don't overwork and try to rest more. When you're resting and asleep, it's better to lay on your side, so as to decrease the pressure on the vena cava from the uterus. Wear comfy clothes which allow you to move freely. Give preference to items with natural fabrics.

baby: Your baby's brain is maturing rapidly; all the cells have already formed; and the increase in neuronal connections supports further growth.The development of the spine is completing; the bone tissue is strengthening; and the vertebra and intervertebral discs are developing. The nervous system is evolving and your baby's movements are no longer that chaotic - they've become more balanced and coordinated.
mom: Blood flow increases, and as a result your red blood cell (erythrocyte) count will be at it's lowest this week. The latter can lead to physiological anaemia, which can be prevented by eating more iron-rich foods. Even though doctors refer to this kind of anaemia as a natural occurrence, it's still best to see a doctor if you have it.Oedema appears as a result of extra fluid in your body. The swelling itself can appear anywhere in your body. Consult your doctor, who will prescribe you the correct treatment as necessary.
helpful_tips: Usually, pain doesn't bother pregnant women so much this week. If it does, it's usually a pain in the legs due to walking; or back pain. If you have calcium and magnesium deficiency, you could have painful seizures in the calves.

baby: Your baby is developing quite well, and will continue to prepare for life outside until their due date. The formation of organs and systems is being completed, and they will continue to grow and develop. Even though the baby will take its first breath right after being born, they are actively preparing their lungs by swallowing and spitting out amniotic fluid and making movements similar to breathing, reaching up to 60 times per minute. Your baby often sleeps and wakes up for a while.
mom: During the second trimester, you may have your first contractions called Braxton-hicks. These contractions are quick tightenings of the uterine muscles, and unlike the real ones are irregular and painless. This is normal, as your body is preparing ahead for labourYou just need to relax and breathe deeply. If the tension goes away, then you have nothing to worry about. As for your baby's kicks, not only you can feel the - you can see them too. If you lay on your back, you'll most likely see small bumps coming out at different parts of your belly. Soon you'll be able to tell when your baby is sleeping, rolling around or playing.
helpful_tips: Try not to lift any heavy objects and don't carry any heavy bags. Don't forget about your well being: you don't need to stress or overwork yourself. If you need to go to the store, take your partner with for help with any heavy lifting. The same applies to household chores - let your loved ones do them. Maybe you should consider antenatal classes.

baby: The respiratory system continues to develop, preparing the lungs for independent breathing. The bronchial tree is fully developed.As for appearance, your baby looks almost the same as how they'll look at birth. Their nose and lips have formed. The eyes and ears are in the right places; the eyelids have eyelashes; and the eyebrows are above the eyes. Your baby is gaining weight, growing and developing, and taking up almost all the free space in the uterus.
mom: Your overall wellbeing is getting much better, and your mood swings are not that intense as they were before. Your hair is becoming thick and shiny, and your skin clean and soft. Although, the opposite might happen and they become dry and brittle.The slight movements of your baby turn into kicking and even punching. You may have abdominal pain as a result - especially if they were kicking their legs.Besides this, during the second trimester you may experience spasms in the foot and calve muscles.This is usually due to calcium, phosphorus, magnum, or potassium deficiency. The growing womb increases pressure on the vessels, and as a result blood circulation to the lower limbs could be compromised, causing them to spasm. If you experience this, you should consult your doctor who'll prescribe you effective treatment.
helpful_tips: Your body is changing, but it doesn't mean that you're becoming less attractive. Pregnancy is natural, and if your partner dreams about having a baby as much as you do, then to them you are the most beautiful woman in the world. He doesn't care about your weight gain or your stretch marks.It's essential and beneficial to stay active during pregnancy and do physical exercises regularly. If you're feeling up to it, go out for a walk, go to the swimming pool, take pregnancy yoga classes or work out on a fit-ball. Light physical exercise helps all your systems to function normally; it contributes to the healthy development of your baby; and also prepares you for upcoming labour.

baby: The skin takes on its natural tone and becomes more elastic. At this point in pregnancy formation of the gonads has completed. And you probably already know who are you expecting. As for boys, their testicles start to descend into the scrotum; and as for girls, they start to form a vagina. Your baby is more active, moving and kicking more often. And their movements become better coordinated. Your baby also reacts to your mood swings; they frown, smile and feel pain. Of course, they smile out of joy and frown out of anger.
mom: Your belly is becoming much more prominent,and you're starting to feel clumsy and slow. The uterus has increased in size, so it pushes onto the diaphragm and subcostal plane, shifting the stomach as result. Besides the discomfort, sometimes gastric acid goes up and enters the oesophagus, causing burning sensations and heartburn. To prevent heartburn, try not to overeat. As your body requires more oxygen and nutrients, the volume of blood in your body constantly increases and you may feel your heart rate go up - especially if you suddenly change position, or when doing physical exercise. You may notice that you breathe more often than you did before becoming pregnant. Significant changes are occurring to your respiratory system, as it now needs oxygen for two. The lungs' capacity increases and the circumference of your chest may grow several inches.
helpful_tips: Try to spend more time out in the fresh air. This way, your body will get more oxygen, which will be beneficial for the baby's development. As your belly grows, heartburn may become intense -especially after a big meal. You can reduce this unpleasant discomfort.

baby: Your baby has grown significantly and continues to develop. Their skin is becoming less wrinkled as the accumulation of adipose tissue makes your baby look more healthy; but they still look skinnier than how they will look after they're born, as the main fat deposits will be built up in the later months of pregnancy. The sensory organs continue to develop. Your baby can already distinguish smells and flavours, and can also hear different sounds - both internal and external. Don't be surprised if your baby punches you after a loud and sudden sound, as this is how your baby shows its displeasure.
mom: All your thoughts are concentrated on preparing for the upcoming birth and your newborn. At this moment, it's essential to eliminate stress and physical exertion; to have the support of your close ones; and to have proper sleep and nutrition.You're having to be more careful when you walk, to avoid the risk of premature birth as a result of falling. Your stomach is lifting higher and higher, and as a result, you might have shortness of breath and the urge to inhale deeply. You may also have heartburn and nausea due to the uterus enlarging. And with increased fluids in your body, you may get oedema not only in your legs but in your face and fingers too. You also might notice changes to your eyesight - it usually gets worse. Fluid retention can change the thickness and shape of the cornea, which can result in worsening vision. Fortunately, in the majority of cases vision restores itself after birth.
helpful_tips: If you are still working, then be sure to go for walks in the evenings. Keep an eye on your diet. Your weight should be within the normal range.Try to exclude high-calorie foods with a low nutritional value from your diet, such as baked goods, pastries, cakes, sweets, and greasy and fried foods. It doesn't mean that a piece of your favourite chocolate bar is prohibited, but that you should not eat too much of it. Exercise regularly.

baby: Your baby can open and close their eyes. The sucking reflex has developed well, and the baby intensely sucks its fingers and toes. Your baby isn't small anymore, but that doesn't stop them from moving around or turning upside down, as there is enough space in the womb for movement. Despite that, your baby's kicks become more noticeable and visible outside by the week - especially when a palm or little heel is popping out of your bump.Although the baby might take up the bottom-down position or maybe even lay transversally across the womb, there's nothing wrong in this as your baby has plenty of time to get into the right position by themself.
mom: As your enlarged uterus is pushing on the stomach and intestines, you might have heartburn and constipation from time to time. The uterus is also pressing on the inferior vena cava, resulting in dizziness.Your breasts adjust to breastfeeding, become more elastic and dense, and the nipples sometimes excrete colostrum.You may not be familiar with meteoropathy, but you may experience it now during your pregnancy. You may notice that you have started to react to changes in the weather, which can affect your wellbeing.The level of Cholesterol in your blood is gradually being raised, but you shouldn't worry about it. Cholesterol is vital for the placenta to produce different types of hormones, such as progesterone, which is crucial for breastfeeding and producing milk.
helpful_tips: More likely than not, the weight you've gained has already affected your looks. Perhaps these changes suit you. Light makeup or a fresh hairstyle can lift your mood - during pregnancy, you can feel free to stay beautiful and desirable. Your outfit should be roomy and loose so that you don't feel any irritation.

baby: The legs and arms have grown; and the body has become proportional to the head - now it doesn't look that big in comparison.Your baby already knows your voice, which will never be mistaken for someone else's. Your baby can feel your mood and hears every word you say.By the way, at this point your baby's eyes are blue; the pigmentation will start to change towards the end of pregnancy. Now your baby is beginning to develop their personal sleeping habits. They might be very active at night, but be the opposite during the day - sleeping and resting more. If you're expecting a girl, all the follicles in her ovaries have already formed. And if you're having a boy, his testicles have already descended into the scrotum.
mom: The skin on your abdomen is stretched, covered with stretch marks and is sometimes itchy. Your breasts are still getting bigger and you might notice some colostrum excretion. The womb has grown significantly and is continuing to grow alongside your baby. If you haven't had Braxton-hicks contractions before, then you might now have these irregular, sporadic contractions of the uterus. Don't worry, this is how the womb is preparing itself for the upcoming birth. The uterus is now so high that it pushes up into the diaphragm, resulting in difficulty breathing and it becomes harder to take a deep breath than before. Sometimes you might have shortness of breath, heartburn, constipation and spasms. It becomes harder to walk because of weight gain and you may feel clumsy. You're getting tired faster, so try to spend less time on your feet.
helpful_tips: Put on comfortable shoes and move your chair back for there to be more space in front of your bump; and try to place a small pillow under your lower back for additional comfort.

baby: Your baby's body is becoming more and more developed, and all the systems are uniting together into a single mechanism. The bone marrow works steadily and produces red blood cells. Your baby has its own immune system, but is still getting the majority of their antibodies from your body.Your baby is less active now, due to having grown and having less space in the womb. However, it will push and kick more intensely, and their kicks will be more noticeable and not that pleasant like they were before.
mom: Your small bump is starting to grow into a big belly, causing you to worry more. Don't worry if your navel is prominent and is popping out, as it will return to normal after giving birth. You might have some unpleasant symptoms, such as shortness of breath, pain in the lower limbs, heartburn and constipation, which will accompany you till the end of pregnancy. As the uterus is pressing down on your bladder, you might have to urinate more frequently at night. That is why you should compensate for any lack of sleep at night with the rest during the day.
helpful_tips: Try to do exercises for pregnant women regularly, and also wear a bandage.During pregnancy, many women suffer from haemorrhoids. To prevent this condition, try to be careful with your diet and make sure to include foods that aid digestion. If haemorrhoids have already appeared, then you should not treat them yourself. You should consult your doctor.

baby: The respiratory system continues to develop. On an ultrasound, you can see how your baby's chest is going up and down as they breathe.As for the skin, it becomes less wrinkled and smooth. The skin will stay covered in protective vernix until birth, and the downy hair (lanugo) holding the vernix to the skin will gradually fade away. At the same time, little hairs grow on their head and become thicker. Their fingers have nails; eyes have eyelashes; and their cheeks become rounded and chubby.
mom: You're continuing to gain some kilograms. Over half of this weight is made up by the uterus, amniotic fluid and placenta. You're becoming more slow and clumsy, and you might notice that it's getting harder to make routine movements.To prevent any unwanted weight gain, you can do some light gymnastics and keep track of your diet. The growing uterus is putting pressure on the organs nearby, lifting them up and decreasing your lung capacity. As a result, you may feel worsening shortness of breath and, due to your stomach shifting upwards, heartburn.Try to avoid making any sudden movements. The abdominal muscles are weak and stretched due to the enlarged uterus, so you should be more careful.
helpful_tips: Now is the perfect time for you to start shopping for baby clothes and things, and to decorate their room or their corner in the bedroom. All this preparation activity of buying stuff for your future baby will cheer you up and bring positive emotions. If you can't go shopping in person, you can switch to online shopping.

baby: The baby continues to grow alongside the growth of its organs.The baby tries to make them self as compact as possible by curling their hands and legs closer to their body and bending their head forward. This way, the baby is getting ready to come out. But it doesn't mean that your baby will sit and wait for its time quietly now. It will still train its muscles, move, shove and kick. Don't forget that all the emotions that you experience are passed on to your baby, as they can feel your mood keenly, and react to your happiness and joy with a smile.
mom: Your body is preparing to give birth, and you're starting to have Braxton-hicks contractions. Have you ever thought about how your baby will come out? Fortunately, your body is secreting the special hormone relaxin, or in other words, the pregnancy hormone. It weakens the cartilage which binds the bones, so that the pelvic bones spread apart to prepare for a normal delivery at birth. Due to physiological changes, painful symptoms are almost inevitable. At this point, you will often feel lower back pain because of your growing belly; loosening ligaments and joints; and also a shifted centre of gravity. Due to the increased load on your legs, you may develop varicose veins. A gentle foot and shin massage might help. Not only is it hard to fall asleep, but you also have to go to the toilet at night, as your bladder is under pressure too. Don't dwell on these changes too much though, as they will go away after birth.
helpful_tips: Try to exercise regularly. Swimming, aqua aerobics or yoga for pregnant women are the most suitable for you at this point. These sports will make you more resilient and stronger, and won't overload your heart and blood vessels at the same time.Keep learning how to relax and mastering proper breathing techniques, as they will come in handy during labour. Try to spend more time outside, being closer to nature and picturesque places. Don't worry about periods when your baby does not move or kick. Perhaps your baby is just resting. But if these periods become prolonged, then you should inform your doctor.

baby: The nervous system of your baby continues to develop. If a beam of bright light is directed to their face through your belly, their pupils will constrict. Your baby can experience pain and emotions, and can have mood swings. They can fully hear, see and feel your attention.Lanugo continues to fall out as there is no need for it anymore, as adipose tissue is now responsible for heat exchange. Lanugo will fall out completely in the first weeks after or right before birth.
mom: The most comforting feeling during pregnancy is your baby kicking of course, and the excitement of the upcoming birth of your precious angel.This week, your growing belly is causing you some problems. If your baby is turned upside down, then their legs are pressing up against the ribs. When the baby moves and kicks, you may experience chest pain. Therefore, try not to bend over and try to sit up straight. Your internal organs have shifted slightly, but it shouldn't bother you. Unlike fluid retention in your body, which can cause swelling in the veins, ankles and fingers. During pregnancy, it's recommended to avoid wearing rings, tight clothes and tight shoes.
helpful_tips: If you have trouble sleeping, then try to change your evening routine. Every night before going to bed, take a walk in the fresh air or listen to relaxing music. If your big belly makes it uncomfortable for you to sleep, then try using a pregnancy pillow. It will be much easier to find a comfortable position with this pillow, and as a result, you'll sleep better. If you are worried about severe oedema due to weight gain, then you should consult your doctor, as severe oedema can indicate preeclampsia.

baby: All parts of the body become proportional, and your baby looks like a newborn already.If for any reason you enter labour prematurely this week, your baby will be able to breathe on its own. However, there isn't enough subcutaneous fat and the skin is still thin. That is why newborns can't maintain their body temperature and keep warmth, and require an incubator.Your baby has already taken up their final position in the womb. The most favourable one is the anterior position when the baby is head-down because the head will be the first thing to come through the birth canal. The breech position, when the baby is lying bottom first, can happen.. In this case, doctors will probably perform a Caesarean to avoid injuring the baby during delivery.
mom: You can increasingly feel labour approaching, and from time to time you may have nervousness and anxiety.Sleep becomes more uncomfortable, and sometimes it's hard to breathe - especially when you lay down.The uterus is pressing on the bladder, causing frequent urination, so you have to wake up and go to the toilet several times at night.
helpful_tips: When you rest, try to avoid lying on your back, as it reduces blood flow to the womb. It is advisable to lie on your left side to improve blood flow. If you want your belly to return to its initial shape more quickly, wear a bandage. It will support the womb, which can also expand the lower abdomen area.

baby: All the organs and systems continue to develop. The G.I. tract has formed and is ready to work independently.Sometimes, your baby might have hiccups, but as you remember this could be as a result of swallowing amniotic fluid - so you don't need to worry about this.The wrinkles go away, and the baby's skin becomes more smooth, lighter and gets a natural tone. The bone tissue continues to develop and get stronger with the help of calcium, which your baby gets from your body.There is less space in the uterus, so your baby tries to push away all your internal organs, hold on to your ribs or bladder, and make them self more comfortable.
mom: The Braxton-hicks are becoming more frequent. Sometimes the tension becomes so intense you could easily confuse them with the real ones. Braxton-hicks contractions may be painful, but they are irregular and last for no longer than 45 seconds. The tightening usually comes from the uterine fundus, before they spread down and fade away. At the same time, you might feel pain in your back. Don't worry, Braxton-hicks contractions are not dangerous and bring no harm to your body.As for your emotional status, the days of frequent mood swings and nervousness are long gone.
helpful_tips: If you suffer from heartburn, try breaking down your diet into six or seven small meals a day, instead of three or four large ones. Try to avoid wearing uncomfortable and tight clothes. Instead, to lower discomfort wear loose ones that don't restrict your movements. A good thing to do is to pre-pack any necessary things for the hospital, because now contractions may occur at the most unexpected time. And when they start, there is no time to think about anything else.

baby: Your baby is growing fast and gaining weight. The hairs on their head are growing rapidly. Of course, some babies are born practically bald, but every case is individual, and is in no small part down to genes. In general, your baby is unique, they have their own fingerprints and their facial features are inimitable. Your baby is getting ready to be born, becoming chubby and adorable.
mom: You may feel tired because of the bigger size of your belly and discomfort it causes. Poor blood circulation causes pain and swelling in the legs. Your growing stomach squeezes the lungs, making it harder to breathe and causing shortness of breath. The skin becomes stretched and itchy, and stretch marks develop. Don't worry if your navel pops out, as it will return back to normal after birth. The womb keeps pressing on the stomach and intestines, causing heartburn.
helpful_tips: During the last stages of pregnancy, women may feel anxious of the unknown - the upcoming birth, to be precise. The most effective way to deal with stress is to collect as much information about what will happen to you during labour as possible. You can discuss this with your doctor and midwife.You should understand that giving birth is not as painful as you think. Besides, as soon as labour starts, fear and anxiety will go away on their own. Moreover, the moment you see your baby you will immediately forget about your pain and worries.

baby: Your baby often sucks their fingers in preparation for breastfeeding. Your child can be considered ready to enter the world. Almost every bone, except for the skull, has already become stronger. It helps the baby to pass through the birth canal without complications.The amount of surfactant accumulated in the lungs is now sufficient enough so that your baby can breathe by itself in case they are born. Before that, they could only breathe through their mouth; but now they are learning to breathe with their nose because they'll need to when eating.
mom: The uterine fundus is at its maximum height, beneath the sternum (breast bone). It's still hard to breathe; you're suffering from heartburn often; and your baby's kicks are more pronounced and painful.Sometimes it may feel like your baby's legs are wiggling right under your heart. Your growing belly often causes lower back pain. You may feel discomfort, and be clumsy and awkward because of your large abdominal size. Of course, you're going to get fed up of it, but you'll have to wait it out, as your womb will soon descend and these symptoms will go away.
helpful_tips: This week, you need to be prepared for the birth of your child. So it's about time to choose the right hospital if you have not already done so. Try not to listen to anyone, especially those who have all sorts of scary things to say about childbirth. Every woman experiences labour differently, and each labour is individual; so even the same woman can have a different experience each time.If you don't have any contraindications, then you can wear a special bandage to relieve back pain. Continue to do special exercises for pregnant women. You'll probably want to check with your doctor, whether it is possible to have sex or not. But one thing is for sure: intimate relations in the later stages of pregnancy can cause premature birth.

baby: Even though your baby is practically ready for birth, their development is still going on. They grow and gain weight.During this week, the hormone Cortizone is being produced, which contributes to the development of the lungs. Right now they are excluded from the blood circulation system, but right after birth (with your baby's first breath) blood will enter the lungs and absorb oxygen.If labour takes place this week, it will be considered full-termbe considered full-term. The birth will not be that big of stress for your baby as its adrenal glands have already produced a special hormone to help them adapt to life in their environment. That is why you shouldn't worry about your baby's health if they're born this week. Your baby can breathe independently, suck on your breasts and digest food. And of course, they can hear and see, as well as distinguish flavours and smells.
mom: The feeling of discomfort is increasing. You may feel clumsy and big, and it seems that even your maternity clothes are becoming tight. Two weeks before you give birth, the uterine fundus descends and your bump will drop. Breathing will become easier; heartburn will become less intense; and the pressure on your chest and stomach will decrease. But considering how the uterus is now pressing harder on your bladder, the urge to go to the bathroom becomes more frequent. Your baby's new position and weight shift your centre of gravity, causing backache. At this point, the Braxton-hicks contractions become more frequent, resembling real contractions more and more each time; and sometimes, your belly feels firm.If the contractions bother you, it's best to go to the doctor.
helpful_tips: Try to relax more and avoid stress. At this stage, it is especially important. Do light gymnastics for pregnant women if you have the strength for it. Continue to eat small portions several times a day. Do not forget about fruit and vegetables, which should be in your diet. If you are giving birth at a hospital, then make sure you have all the necessary things for the hospital.

baby: All the baby's organs are fully formed and ready to work and function outside the womb. Sometimes meconium is excreted before birth. In this case, the meconium will come out alongside the waters, which could be green coloured. There is nothing wrong with this, as it won't cause any harm to your baby's health. There's practically no free space left in the womb, so your baby has become less active - even small movements are more perceptible to you.
mom: As labour approaches, you feel more and more tired, as well as potentially anxious and scared of the upcoming birth. You shouldn't worry about it though, but rather think about how each coming day is getting you closer to the moment when you will get to hold your baby in your arms, and put him or her on your chest. Besides the physical exertion and emotional anxiety, you may still have Braxton-hicks contractions, backache and oedema.
helpful_tips: At this stage, it is better to avoid long outings and being far from home, because labour can start at any time. Do something nice and pleasant for yourself every day. For example, you could take a walk in the park, watch a funny movie or read an interesting book. Enjoy this period to the fullest, because in the coming weeks or even months after the birth, you won't have any time for this.

baby: The sucking reflex develops more, and chewing skills will appear right after their first feed. In the later stages of pregnancy, the baby practically doesn't make any movement due to the decrease in amniotic fluid. Your baby is taking up all available space in the womb, making it harder for them to turn around. Therefore, your baby's position is probably their final one and won't change any more. If your baby is sitting bottom-down, don't worry. Babies can be born vaginally when in the breech, but doctors nowadays prefer to perform a Cesarean to minimize the risks, which won't cause any complications to you and your baby.
mom: From the beginning of your pregnancy, your overall weight and abdominal size have increased. As a result, you might have developed stretch marks on your skin. But you shouldn't worry about them, as they will fade away after some time and become unnoticeable on your skin. The uterus is pressing harder onto your bladder, and it seems like you're always having to go to the toilet, especially at night, so try to avoid excessive fluid intake in the evenings. If your bump has dropped, you might notice the load on your pelvis and spine has increased, and as a result, it becomes harder to walk, and sit, and even impossible to find a comfortable sleep position. But there are positive moments it becomes easier to breathe and heartburn fades away, as the belly no longer presses on the lungs and stomach.
helpful_tips: Try to massage the perineum and do perineal exercises at least a few times a day. These simple exercises can help you avoid injuries during labour. In the last weeks of pregnancy, it is essential to rest more. Try to eat small portions frequently. If you already have children, try to maintain a trusting relationship with them. Explain that you won't love them any less when a brother or sister comes to the family.

baby: Your baby has grown significantly and gained weight. There's not enough space in the womb anymore to make any active movements and they don't want to wait anymore. Your baby is completely prepared to enter the world. All their vital organs are developed and ready to work independently. Your baby has taken the foetal position, their head pushing towards the birth canal; and their legs and arms bent and pressed against their belly. After your baby has come through the birth canal the doctor will cut off the umbilical cord. Your baby will be cleaned and wrapped in a warm, sterile blanket to keep their body warm as they aren't fully able to regulate their temperature yet. Then the doctor will evaluate your newborn's condition in the first minutes of their life using the Apgar scale. This is a simple method used to determine whether they will need resuscitation. The scale includes a summary analysis of five parameters, including: skin colour, heart rate, reflexes, muscle tone and breathing effort.The Apgar scale is one of three criteria, including weight and height, which the doctor will tell you about after your baby is born.
mom: This week your body is preparing for labour - your bones are softening, and your ligaments and joints are stretching. As a result back pain may intensify, and your gait may become more clumsy. Due to the increased size of your belly, it becomes harder and harder to sleep. Try to find a comfortable position and air out your room before going to bed. Be attentive to your baby's movements and go to the doctor if they are too active or on the contrary, become less intense. This week, you might notice the mucus plug coming out, meaning that labour can start at any time. Your waters breaking are also a precursor to labour. Your waters may break quickly or gradually. Either way, be attentive and go to the doctor if you feel anything suspicious.
helpful_tips: Check whether all the necessary things for the hospital have been packed. Put them in a prominent place in your house. Despite the growing anxiety and discomfort, try to walk outside and do some exercise. Talk to your doctor about all the signs that labour is nearing.Remember all the moments that you have experienced during your pregnancy. If you have taken photos of this wonderful period, then after a while they will make you smile and reminisce. And you'll be able to show the pictures to your grown-up baby, to let them know how they lived and grew in your belly.

baby: Your baby weighs more than 3 kg at this point and is still continuing to grow. The hair and nails don't stop growing, and your baby might scratch themself during the labour. All their organs, including their heart, liver, kidneys and pancreas, are functional and work well.Your baby's first faeces (meconium) are being stored in the colon, which will be excreted right after birth. It's getting tighter in the belly day by day and your baby's movements are restricted - their kicks becoming more intense as result.
mom: One week early, one week late - neither are especially a cause for concern for doctors. Doctors will only offer to induce labour or a Cesarean section if your pregnancy has extended beyond the due date.
helpful_tips: Try not to think about contractions. These thoughts will only make you more anxious. Do not forget about your diet and make sure to walk in the fresh air. Try to rest more and enjoy your life, as it will definitely change after the birth of your child.

baby: Your baby continues to grow and gain weight this week. In general, everything is fine except that the large foetus is less mobile and won't get through the birth canal that easily. At the same time, the majority of babies at this stage are born healthy and developed.
mom: Haven't you given birth yet? 10% of all pregnant women carry their babies before this week. Don't worry if you're one of them. Everyone's body is different, and perhaps this due date is normal for yours. But it's recommended to not wait too long and consult a doctor.
helpful_tips: This week, tests are done as directed by a doctor. If you have not given birth yet, then you should be prepared for the fact that the doctor may offer to induce labour or perform a Caesarean section. Don't worry.
